Commentary.Commentary: It still looks like a pace-friendly pitch and we are already in the third innings in the First Session of Day 2. The skies are pretty much clear with the sun peeking out of the scattered clouds. This could very well be another low-scoring innings but it's more exciting to watch some good cricketing action.

We are back for the third innings. The umpires walk out to the middle followed by Tony de Zorzi and Aiden Markram, the opening batters for South Africa. Jayden Seales has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Right then, South Africa are 16 runs after the end of the first inning, and would expect an improved batting performance this time around. West Indies after showing a relentless fight with the bat, would like to replicate their performance with the ball like they did earlier. This Test match has progressed at a rapid pace, and with ample time remaining, a definitive result is inevitable. Stay tuned, as the South African inning, commences shortly.

South Africa's bowling attack proved potent, with Wiaan Mulder and Nandre Burger sharing 7 wickets between them. The Proteas' pacers, including Kagiso Rabada, consistently challenged the hosts with varied lines and clever setups. Keshav Maharaj also made his mark, taking a wicket to bring the first day to a close. As play resumed on day two, Rabada and Burger maintained their stranglehold, each adding another wicket to their tally. The West Indies' innings could have concluded at a mere 104 runs, had Aiden Markram not dropped a straightforward catch in the slips. As a result, the salt on the wounds were sprayed by Joseph's relentless counterattack. However, the ploy to summon Keshav Maharaj worked for the Proteas as he wrapped up things taking two to his name.

Phew, what an engrossing play we have had in this first session. Yes, it's a low-scoring affair, but to say the least, it has been a sheer entertainer. After an underwhelming batting performance on Day 1, the dawn of a new day brought a crucial test for the West Indies, who needed to carefully navigate the opening hour. However, their plans were quickly derailed as they lost two wickets within the first 10 overs. Amidst this adversity, Shamar Joseph, after running a riot with the ball, emerged as an unexpected spark with the bat, alongside Jason Holder who notched up his valiant 50. Despite being dropped twice, Joseph adopted an aggressive approach playing some audacious shots to the fence. Joseph and Holder together added 40 runs which shrank the deficit to 16 runs in a rapid time.

Commentary.Commentary: Well then, all set for Day 2 to get underway at the Providence Stadium, Guyana! The umpires are punctual and out to the middle. South African players are in the huddle near the ropes discussing the last-minute strategies before spreading out to their fielding positions. Jason Holder, unbeaten on 33, will resume his inning and Jomel Warrican will join him at number 9, as Day 1 wrapped up with the wicket of Gudakesh Motie. Keshav Maharaj (4.2-1-6-1) will start the proceedings and will bowl the remaining four deliveries of his fifth over. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Vernon Philander and Nikhil Uttamchandani are inspecting the deck before the Day 2 commences. Nikhil Uttamchandani begins by saying that the outfield is lightning-quick. Vernon Philander joins him and says the surface is rock-hard and the seamers will get a lot of movement. Adds that the roots of the grass on the surface will help the seamers to generate that lateral movement. Expects it to be yet another entertaining day of play.

The West Indies, still 63 runs behind, exactly the figure of South Africa's 10th wicket partnership, will look upon their seasoned all-rounder Jason Holder to provide stubborn resistance, but a responsible hand from the other end is also crucial. However, the opening hour of play could prove pivotal, as is often the case in Test cricket. Also, it will be interesting to see how the track behaves this time around. South Africa's formidable pace attack will aim to exploit the new ball, seeking early breakthroughs to deny the home team any chance of gaining the upper hand. A riveting day is up on the cards, folks! The first ball of Day 2 will be bowled at 7.30 pm IST (1400 GMT). Stay tuned.

A mirroring trend was seen on the opening day, as the new ball did a lot of mischief and left the batters unanswerable. However, as the ball softened and lost its bite, and the pitch evened out, batting became noticeably easier as the day wore on. Looking ahead to Day 2, we can expect much of the same, with minimal chances of rain in the forecast around noon. Conditions are expected to remain largely identical, with sunny skies prevailing for most of the day, and the remaining match days.

But also, we did see some batting resiliencies amid the procession of wickets. South Africa’s 10th wicket stand that added 63 runs between Dane Piedt and Burger kind of frustrated the West Indian bowlers for a fair bit and helped the Proteas to 160 after being 9 down on a paltry 97. Early contributions from Stubbs, Bedingham, and Verreynee proved to be crucial but they couldn’t extend their starts to a big score. Dane Piedt proved why he can be a handy component as an all-rounder. The spicy deck was no different for the hosts as they were reduced to 97/7 but this collapse was followed by the gutsy stand between Jason Holder and Gudakesh Motie when the chips were down.

Shamar Joseph, the local lad, lit up the match with a sensational 5-wicket haul, keeping the contest wide open and bringing the West Indies right into the thick of it.
